ExampleDefinition.ToolTipDescription: Demonstrates how to use SciChart, specifically a Polar Uniform Heatmap to visualize real-world heatmap data.
ExampleDefinition.Description:
This example demonstrates how to create a Polar Uniform Heatmap using SciChart to visualize real-world maximum daily temperature data over multiple years.
The PolarXAxis (Angular Axis) represents the days of the year and is divided into sector-like grid lines that mark month boundaries, with month labels positioned at the center of each sector. The PolarYAxis (Radial Axis) represents individual years and is segmented using circular grid lines.
[b]Data Input[/b] The heatmap accepts a 2D array of maximum daily temperature values, where each row corresponds to a year and each column represents a day of the year. Each year is assumed to contain 366 days; for non-leap years, the value corresponding to February 29 is represented as NaN. Missing measurements are represented as NaN values in the dataset and are rendered as transparent cells.
[b]Chart Legend[/b] A color map is applied to translate temperature values into visually distinct colors. This enables intuitive interpretation of seasonal gradients, extreme temperature peaks, and long-term trends within the data. It is visually represented by a ColorMap control displayed as a chart legend.
[b]Interactivity[/b] Interactions allow users to explore year-round temperature patterns in detail: - Tooltips displaying calendar dates and temperature values - Rubber-band zooming along angular and radial axes - Mouse-wheel zooming - Chart export functionality - A legend for interpreting the color scale
